This lesson is for a pianist who can play triads. It puts the chords of [the lesson on C, Am, F, G](pop-changes.qmd) on the keyboard: a left-hand root and a close-position chord in the right hand. Each step has a keyboard diagram, the chart and a grand staff, and the band plays along.

**How to use the page.** Press ▶ on a chart and the band plays it four times after a one-bar count-in. The bar that is sounding lights up, on the chart and on the staff. Under every chord is its Roman numeral, which stays the same in every key. The strip at the bottom of the window sets the key, the feel, the tempo and the chord instrument, and you can change them while the band plays. Shaded bars are the ones that differ from the version named under the chart.

## 1. The basic chords

**C, Am, F, G.** The keyboard diagram shows one lane for each chord: the left-hand root (square) and a right-hand chord above it. The staff under the chart shows the same notes: treble clef for the right hand, bass clef for the left.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="basic"></div>

## 2. Extensions

**Cadd9, Am7, Fadd9, Gsus2.** The right hand keeps its shape and adds one note. Look for the 9 or the 7 in the diagram.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="ext"></div>

## 3. Passing chords

**C, G/B | Am, C/G | F, F♯dim | G.** The left hand walks: C, B, A, G, F, F♯, G. Each right-hand chord changes only where it has to.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="pass"></div>

## 4. Secondary dominants

**C, E7 | Am, C7 | F, D7 | G7.** The chord with the outside note leads by half step into the next bar.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="sec"></div>

## 5. The two-five-one

**Dm7, G7, Cmaj7.** The most common move in jazz and in many pop bridges: the chord before the dominant, the dominant, home. The left-hand roots fall a fifth each time (D, G, C). In the right hand, look for the note that stays and the one that moves by a half step: the F of Dm7 is the 7th of G7, and it falls to the E, the 3rd of Cmaj7.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="251"></div>

## 6. The two-five-one in minor

**Dm7♭5, G7, Cm7.** The same fall in C minor. The first chord is half-diminished: a minor triad with a flat 5th and a 7th (D, F, A♭, C). Compare it with Dm7 above: one note has moved down a half step.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="251m"></div>

## Build your own

Pick a chord for each bar. The keyboard diagram and the staff follow your choices. Try Dm7 and G7 in bars 3 and 4.

<div id="bl-builder" class="bl-widget"></div>


## Test your ear

The band plays four bars with one of five kinds of change in them. Say which. The chart appears when you answer.

<div id="bl-quiz" class="bl-widget"></div>

## Where to go next

- Move to another key with the strip and watch which keys the right hand lands on.
- Try the same steps with [guide tones](guide-tones.qmd) in the right hand: only the 3rd and 7th of each chord.
